nodes.title: Regex-denoted languages are closed under union

nodes.summary: A singleton `{[a]}` is denoted by `char a`.
nodes.title: Single-letter languages are regex-denoted

nodes.summary: The system of equations of a DFA at a state: the coefficient of `X j` in the equation for `X q`, the finite union of the singletons `{[a]}` over the letters taking `q` to `j`.
nodes.title: Coefficient in the equation system of a DFA

nodes.summary: The constant term of the equation for `X q`: `1` on accepting states, `0` otherwise.
nodes.title: Constant term in the equation system of a DFA

nodes.summary: Every coefficient is denoted by a regular expression.
nodes.title: DFA equation coefficients are regex-denoted

nodes.summary: Every constant term is denoted by a regular expression.
nodes.title: DFA equation constant terms are regex-denoted

nodes.summary: The coefficient of the reduced system obtained by eliminating the last state: the old coefficient, plus the detour through the last state, which may loop there any number of times.
nodes.title: Coefficient after eliminating the last state

nodes.summary: The constant term of the reduced system obtained by eliminating the last state.
nodes.title: Constant term after eliminating the last state

nodes.summary: The language of a DFA with `Fin n` states is denoted by a regular expression.
nodes.title: Languages of DFAs on finitely many numbered states are regex-denoted

nodes.summary: The language of a DFA over a finite state type is denoted by a regular expression.
nodes.title: Kleene's theorem: DFA languages are regex-denoted

nodes.summary: If the languages `X i` satisfy `X i = (∑ j, A i j * X j) + B i` with every coefficient `A i j` excluding the empty word and every coefficient and constant term denoted by a regular expression, then every `X i` is denoted by a regular expression. The proof eliminates the last state with Arden's lemma and applies the induction hypothesis to the reduced system.
nodes.title: Solving a system of language equations

nodes.summary: Kleene's theorem, converse direction (Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*, 3rd ed., Theorem 1.54): every regular language over a finite alphabet is denoted by a regular expression. Source: M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*, 3rd ed., Theorem 1.54.
nodes.title: Kleene's theorem, converse direction

nodes.summary: Over an infinite alphabet, the language of one-letter words is regular but is denoted by no regular expression, since a regular expression mentions only finitely many letters. Source: M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*, 3rd ed., Theorem 1.54 (finite alphabet).
nodes.title: Sharpness of the finite-alphabet hypothesis

nodes.summary: The DFA equations: from `q`, either step on a letter and continue, or stop if `q` accepts.
nodes.title: Equation system satisfied by DFA state languages

nodes.summary: The language accepted from a state: the unknown `X q` of the system.
nodes.title: Language accepted from a DFA state

nodes.summary: A language is denoted by a regular expression when it is `r.matches'` for some `r`.
nodes.title: Language denoted by a regular expression

nodes.summary: Kleene's theorem (Sipser, 3rd ed., Theorem 1.54): over a finite alphabet, a language is regular if and only if it is denoted by a regular expression. Source: M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*, 3rd ed., Theorem 1.54.
nodes.title: Kleene's theorem

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
